quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: Marcus said to Elena, "I'll carry your bags."
quests.reportedSpeech: Marcus offered to carry her bags.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'I'll carry your bags' becomes 'offered to carry her bags'; the possessive changes to match Elena.
quests.nativeTip: 'I'll do something for you' is a classic offer — use 'offered to' plus the base verb.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Marcus said to Elena, "I'll carry your bags."" ➔ "Marcus offered to carry her bags."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The waiter said, "I can bring you some more bread."
quests.reportedSpeech: The waiter offered to bring some more bread.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'I can bring you...' becomes 'offered to bring'; 'suggested' would require a different structure.
quests.nativeTip: 'Suggested' isn't followed by 'to' + verb — 'offered to' is the correct pattern here.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The waiter said, "I can bring you some more bread."" ➔ "The waiter offered to bring some more bread."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: Priya said to her neighbor, "Do you want me to water your plants while you're away?"
quests.reportedSpeech: Priya offered to water her neighbor's plants while she was away.
changesList: 'do you want me to water' → 'offered to water'
quests.ruleExplanation: The offer 'Do you want me to water...?' becomes 'offered to water', and 'you're' becomes 'she was'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Do you want me to...?' is a polite way of offering — report it with 'offered to'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Priya said to her neighbor, "Do you want me to water your plants while you're away?"" ➔ "Priya offered to water her neighbor's plants while she was away."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Gerund Structure
quests.directSpeech: Layla said, "Let's try the new restaurant downtown."
quests.reportedSpeech: Layla suggested trying the new restaurant downtown.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Let's try' becomes the gerund form 'suggested trying'; 'suggested to try' is a common but incorrect pattern.
quests.nativeTip: 'Suggested' is followed by a gerund (-ing form), not 'to' + verb.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Layla said, "Let's try the new restaurant downtown."" ➔ "Layla suggested trying the new restaurant downtown."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Gerund Structure
quests.directSpeech: The teacher said, "Why don't we review the material together?"
quests.reportedSpeech: The teacher suggested reviewing the material together.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Why don't we review...?' becomes 'suggested reviewing', following the gerund pattern.
quests.nativeTip: 'Why don't we...?' is a common way to suggest something — use the gerund after 'suggested'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The teacher said, "Why don't we review the material together?"" ➔ "The teacher suggested reviewing the material together."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Gerund Structure
quests.directSpeech: Diego said, "How about taking a break?"
quests.reportedSpeech: Diego suggested taking a break.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'How about taking...?' becomes 'suggested taking', keeping the gerund form.
quests.nativeTip: 'How about...?' is another suggestion phrase reported the same way.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Diego said, "How about taking a break?"" ➔ "Diego suggested taking a break."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The consultant said to Hassan, "You should reduce your expenses."
quests.reportedSpeech: The consultant suggested that Hassan reduce his expenses.
quests.ruleExplanation: This is the subjunctive pattern 'suggested that + subject + base verb', so 'reduce' stays unconjugated even with a third-person subject.
quests.nativeTip: After 'suggested that', use the base form of the verb, not the past or present simple form.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The consultant said to Hassan, "You should reduce your expenses."" ➔ "The consultant suggested that Hassan reduce his expenses."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The board said to the manager, "You should submit the proposal by Monday."
quests.reportedSpeech: The board suggested that the manager submit the proposal by Monday.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Submit' stays in its base form after 'suggested that', regardless of the subject.
quests.nativeTip: Same subjunctive rule applies here — don't add '-s' or '-ed' to the verb.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The board said to the manager, "You should submit the proposal by Monday."" ➔ "The board suggested that the manager submit the proposal by Monday."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The doctor said to the patient, "You should see a specialist."
quests.reportedSpeech: The doctor suggested that the patient see a specialist.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'See' remains unconjugated after 'suggested that the patient', following the subjunctive pattern.
quests.nativeTip: Apply the subjunctive rule one more time: base verb after 'suggested that'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The doctor said to the patient, "You should see a specialist."" ➔ "The doctor suggested that the patient see a specialist."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: Isabella said to Marcus, "Would you like to come to my birthday party?"
quests.reportedSpeech: Isabella invited Marcus to come to her birthday party.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Would you like to come...?' becomes 'invited Marcus to come', and 'my' becomes 'her'.
quests.nativeTip: A polite invitation like 'Would you like to...?' is best reported with 'invited...to'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Isabella said to Marcus, "Would you like to come to my birthday party?"" ➔ "Isabella invited Marcus to come to her birthday party."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The company said to the candidates, "Please join us for a final interview."
quests.reportedSpeech: The company invited the candidates to join them for a final interview.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Please join us' becomes 'invited...to join them', matching the tone of an invitation.
quests.nativeTip: Since this is a formal invitation, 'invited' fits better than a plain 'told'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The company said to the candidates, "Please join us for a final interview."" ➔ "The company invited the candidates to join them for a final interview."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: Grace said to her colleagues, "Why don't you all come over for dinner on Saturday?"
quests.reportedSpeech: Grace invited her colleagues to come over for dinner on Saturday.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Why don't you all come...?' becomes 'invited...to come', since this functions as an invitation.
quests.nativeTip: 'Why don't you...?' used to invite someone is reported with 'invited...to', not 'suggested'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Grace said to her colleagues, "Why don't you all come over for dinner on Saturday?"" ➔ "Grace invited her colleagues to come over for dinner on Saturday."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: Hassan said, "I will pay you back next week."
quests.reportedSpeech: Hassan promised to pay her back the following week.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'I will pay you back' becomes 'promised to pay her back', and 'next week' becomes 'the following week'.
quests.nativeTip: A firm commitment like 'I will...' is naturally reported with 'promised to'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Hassan said, "I will pay you back next week."" ➔ "Hassan promised to pay her back the following week."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The contractor said, "I'll finish the renovation by June."
quests.reportedSpeech: The contractor promised to finish the renovation by June.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'I'll finish...' becomes 'promised to finish', reflecting the commitment in the original statement.
quests.nativeTip: This is a firm commitment, not a favor — 'promised' fits better than 'offered'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The contractor said, "I'll finish the renovation by June."" ➔ "The contractor promised to finish the renovation by June."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The children said, "We won't make any noise."
quests.reportedSpeech: The children promised not to make any noise.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Won't make' becomes 'promised not to make', keeping the negative-infinitive pattern.
quests.nativeTip: Keep 'not' directly before 'to' in this negative promise.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The children said, "We won't make any noise."" ➔ "The children promised not to make any noise."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: Ravi said, "Okay, I will help you move this weekend."
quests.reportedSpeech: Ravi agreed to help her move that weekend.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Okay, I will help...' becomes 'agreed to help', and 'this weekend' becomes 'that weekend'.
quests.nativeTip: Saying 'okay' to a request or plan usually becomes 'agreed to'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Ravi said, "Okay, I will help you move this weekend."" ➔ "Ravi agreed to help her move that weekend."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The union said, "We accept the new terms."
quests.reportedSpeech: The union agreed to accept the new terms.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'We accept the new terms' becomes 'agreed to accept the new terms'.
quests.nativeTip: 'We accept...' as a decision reached is best reported with 'agreed to'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The union said, "We accept the new terms."" ➔ "The union agreed to accept the new terms."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Mixed Reported Speech
quests.directSpeech: Both companies said, "We will merge our operations."
quests.reportedSpeech: Both companies agreed to merge their operations.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Our' becomes 'their', and 'we will merge' becomes 'agreed to merge'.
quests.nativeTip: Update the possessive pronoun as well as the reporting verb pattern.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Both companies said, "We will merge our operations."" ➔ "Both companies agreed to merge their operations."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The employee said, "I won't work on weekends."
quests.reportedSpeech: The employee refused to work on weekends.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'I won't work' becomes 'refused to work', capturing the firm rejection.
quests.nativeTip: A firm rejection like 'I won't...' is reported with 'refused to'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The employee said, "I won't work on weekends."" ➔ "The employee refused to work on weekends."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The tenant said, "I will not pay the extra fee."
quests.reportedSpeech: The tenant refused to pay the extra fee.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'I will not pay' becomes 'refused to pay', matching the tenant's rejection.
quests.nativeTip: This is a rejection, not an agreement — check the meaning before picking the reporting verb.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The tenant said, "I will not pay the extra fee."" ➔ "The tenant refused to pay the extra fee."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The witness said, "I won't answer that question."
quests.reportedSpeech: The witness refused to answer that question.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'I won't answer' becomes 'refused to answer'; the refusal itself already carries the negative meaning.
quests.nativeTip: Keep the infinitive form 'to answer' — don't add an extra negative.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The witness said, "I won't answer that question."" ➔ "The witness refused to answer that question."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The manager said, "I will cover your shift tomorrow."
quests.reportedSpeech: The manager offered to cover her shift the next day.
quests.ruleExplanation: Offering to do something as a favor fits 'offered to', while 'promised' suggests a stronger, longer commitment.
quests.nativeTip: This is a spontaneous favor, not a firm long-term commitment — which reporting verb fits best?
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The manager said, "I will cover your shift tomorrow."" ➔ "The manager offered to cover her shift the next day."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The board members said, "We accept your resignation."
quests.reportedSpeech: The board members agreed to accept the resignation.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'We accept...' reflects a decision, matching the pattern 'agreed to accept'.
quests.nativeTip: This is a formal decision that was reached, not a favor or a suggestion.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The board members said, "We accept your resignation."" ➔ "The board members agreed to accept the resignation."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The union leader said, "We will not accept a pay cut."
quests.reportedSpeech: The union leader refused to accept a pay cut.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'We will not accept' becomes 'refused to accept', matching the firm rejection.
quests.nativeTip: This is a firm rejection, not an agreement or a suggestion.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The union leader said, "We will not accept a pay cut."" ➔ "The union leader refused to accept a pay cut."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Gerund Structure
quests.directSpeech: Sofia said, "Let's postpone the launch."
quests.reportedSpeech: Sofia suggested postponing the launch.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Let's postpone' becomes 'suggested postponing'; 'suggested to postpone' is a common learner error.
quests.nativeTip: 'Let's...' proposals use the gerund pattern after 'suggested'.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Sofia said, "Let's postpone the launch."" ➔ "Sofia suggested postponing the launch."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: Andres said, "I'll handle the client communication."
quests.reportedSpeech: Andres offered to handle the client communication.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'I'll handle...' becomes 'offered to handle', since Andres is volunteering, not proposing an idea to others.
quests.nativeTip: This is a spontaneous offer to take on a task, not a suggestion for the group.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Andres said, "I'll handle the client communication."" ➔ "Andres offered to handle the client communication."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The whole team said, "We accept this new plan."
quests.reportedSpeech: The whole team agreed to accept the new plan.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'We accept this new plan' becomes 'agreed to accept the new plan'; 'this' becomes 'the' since it's now a shared reference.
quests.nativeTip: This final decision by the group fits the same pattern you practiced earlier for reaching agreement.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The whole team said, "We accept this new plan."" ➔ "The whole team agreed to accept the new plan."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Gerund Structure
quests.directSpeech: The host said, "Why don't you stay for one more drink?"
quests.reportedSpeech: The host suggested staying for one more drink.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Why don't you stay?' becomes 'suggested staying', following the gerund structure.
quests.nativeTip: Recall the gerund pattern for 'suggested', not the infinitive.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The host said, "Why don't you stay for one more drink?"" ➔ "The host suggested staying for one more drink."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Mixed Reported Speech
quests.directSpeech: Nadia said, "I'll drive you to the airport tomorrow."
quests.reportedSpeech: Nadia offered to drive him to the airport the next day.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'I'll drive you...' becomes 'offered to drive him', and 'tomorrow' becomes 'the next day'.
quests.nativeTip: Think about whether this is a spontaneous favor or a firm long-term commitment.
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "Nadia said, "I'll drive you to the airport tomorrow."" ➔ "Nadia offered to drive him to the airport the next day."

quests.conceptTitle: Speech Bubble to Report Converter: Reporting Verb Pattern
quests.directSpeech: The committee said, "We will not approve this budget."
quests.reportedSpeech: The committee refused to approve the budget.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'We will not approve' becomes 'refused to approve', matching the committee's firm rejection.
quests.nativeTip: This final review question checks a firm rejection — which reporting verb captures that meaning?
quests.backshiftSummary: 🔄 Quote ➔ Report: "The committee said, "We will not approve this budget."" ➔ "The committee refused to approve the budget."
